snippets.output: Although a 35-year-old woman with Hashimoto thyroiditis has a TSH of 28 µIU/mL, this is on the higher end of the stated 9–30 µIU/mL baseline range for Hashimoto thyroiditis.
A cycle day 3 FSH level of 49 mIU/mL in this 35-year-old woman with irregular menstruation suggests primary ovarian insufficiency or menopause.
Elevated FSH levels are indicative of decreased ovarian function and decreased ovarian follicle reserve.
A low estradiol level of 8 pg/mL in this 35-year-old woman supports the diagnosis of primary ovarian insufficiency or menopause and indicates reduced ovarian estrogen production.
In this 35-year-old woman with irregular menstruation, a prolactin level of 14 ng/mL and a testosterone level of 42 ng/dL rule out hyperprolactinemia and significant androgen excess.
Given a 35-year-old woman with irregular menstruation, elevated cycle day 3 FSH of 49 mIU/mL, and low estradiol of 8 pg/mL, the most likely diagnosis is primary ovarian insufficiency (POI).

Brain MRI is not indicated in this 35-year-old woman with irregular menstruation because her prolactin level is normal, there is no evidence of hyperprolactinemia, and she has no neurological symptoms suggestive of a pituitary issue.
Combined oral contraceptives can help regulate menstrual cycles.

Combined oral contraceptives are not the first-line treatment for managing primary ovarian insufficiency symptoms in this 35-year-old woman with irregular menstruation, elevated cycle day 3 FSH, and low estradiol; the most appropriate next step is an estradiol patch with oral medroxyprogesterone.

Hormone replacement therapy with estrogen and progestin is appropriate for managing primary ovarian insufficiency in this 35-year-old woman with irregular menstruation, elevated FSH, and low estradiol.

In a 35-year-old woman with primary ovarian insufficiency, hormone replacement therapy with an estradiol patch and oral medroxyprogesterone relieves primary ovarian insufficiency symptoms by replacing the hormones that the ovaries are no longer producing.
Hormone replacement therapy prevents the long-term consequences of estrogen deficiency in this 35-year-old woman with irregular menstruation, elevated FSH, and low estradiol.
A 35-year-old woman with Hashimoto thyroiditis who takes levothyroxine daily has a TSH level within the normal range for her condition, so adjusting her thyroid medication is unnecessary.

Vaginal estradiol gel can help with local symptoms of vaginal atrophy, but vaginal estradiol gel alone is not sufficient to manage the systemic symptoms of primary ovarian insufficiency in this 35-year-old woman with irregular menstruation, elevated FSH, and low estradiol.

The most appropriate next step in management for this 35-year-old woman with irregular menstruation, elevated FSH, and low estradiol is hormone replacement therapy with an estradiol patch and oral medroxyprogesterone.
